title: Fulvestrant · injections every 4 weeks
context_label: Postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
schedule_summary: NCCP schedule: 500 mg on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of each 28-day cycle. This means Day 29 next, then every 28 days.
purpose: The aim is to control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer and its symptoms, with response and tolerability reviewed before continuing.
indication_text: The NCCP monotherapy card covers postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with relapse or progression in its specified prior anti-oestrogen setting. Companion CDK4/6 medicines require their own regimen.
administration_text: Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile. Confirm the indication, menopausal state, liver category, pregnancy exclusion and any bleeding / anticoagulant risk before intramuscular injections. Liver profile as clinically indicated. At injection visits review symptoms, bleeding / bruising and injection-site or nerve symptoms; response imaging follows the cancer-control plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Fulvestrant
agents.mechanism: Blocks and reduces oestrogen receptors in cancer cells
visual: Receptors are reduced and signalling falls
agents.explanation: Fulvestrant is an endocrine medicine given into muscle. It blocks oestrogen receptors and promotes their breakdown. It is not an intravenous chemotherapy infusion; an accompanying targeted medicine, if prescribed, has its own safety plan.
agents.watch: Report injection pain with numbness or radiating leg pain, extensive bruising, jaundice or worsening symptoms.
risks: Injection-site pain and uncommon nerve injury
Liver enzyme changes or liver injury
Bleeding / bruising risk with intramuscular injections

urgent_extra: Tell the team about unusual bleeding or extensive bruising, injection-site pain with numbness or pain down the leg, jaundice or worsening symptoms. Severe chest pain, breathlessness or stroke symptoms require emergency help.

sections.title: The first month is different
sections.text: There is an extra injection visit two weeks after the first dose. After the Day 29 dose, visits continue every 28 days. Ask the team to confirm each appointment.

sections.title: Before an injection
sections.text: Tell staff about anticoagulants, unusual bleeding or bruising. Do not stop an anticoagulant yourself. The team reviews injection safety and any dose modification.

sections.title: Injection technique and aftercare
sections.text: Staff give deep intramuscular gluteal injections slowly. Report severe pain, numbness or pain radiating down the leg promptly.

sections.title: If a visit is delayed
sections.text: Contact the clinic to agree the next date. Do not calculate a catch-up or extra dose from this reference graphic; dose scheduling remains the clinical team’s responsibility.

evidence.title: CONFIRM: fulvestrant 500 mg versus 250 mg
evidence.population: 736 postmenopausal women with ER-positive locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer after prior endocrine therapy.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Original trial: progression-free survival. This publication reports final overall survival at 75.3% mortality maturity.
evidence.interpretation: Median OS 26.4 versus 22.3 months; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.69–0.96), nominalp=.02, for 500 mg versus 250 mg.
evidence.limitations: Dose-comparison trial, not evidence against current CDK 4/6 combinations. Final OS testing had no multiplicity adjustment. The 250 mg comparator is a historical standard-dose arm, not evidence to override an individual hepatic dose adjustment.

additional_evidence.title: FALCON: separately labelled endocrine-naive context
additional_evidence.population: 462 postmenopausal endocrine-therapy-naive women with HR-positive/HER 2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer.
additional_evidence.interpretation: Fulvestrant 500 mg versus anastrozole 1 mg: median PFS 16.6 versus 13.8 months, HR 0.797 (95% CI 0.637–0.999).
additional_evidence.limitations: Endocrine-naive population differs from NCCP 00361's listed post-adjuvant anti-oestrogen relapse/progression indications. This trial does not broaden the card's prescribing eligibility.

additional_evidence.title: FALCON final overall survival
additional_evidence.population: Same randomized 462-patient FALCON population; final OS 68% mature.
additional_evidence.primary_endpoint: Prespecified final overall-survival analysis; not formally powered for OS.
additional_evidence.interpretation: No significant OS difference:44.8 versus 42.7 months; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.77–1.21),p=.7579.
additional_evidence.limitations: Nonvisceral subgroup signal was not statistically significant. Do not claim a proven OS advantage. Reviewed 2025 erratum corrects author qualifications, not outcomes.

teachback: What is your treatment schedule, which checks apply to your setting, and who books and reviews them?
consent_support: NCCP specifies 250 mg for Child-Pugh B, whereas EMA Faslodex product information describes no mild/moderate reduction with caution. The clinician and pharmacist must reconcile this source difference. Severe hepatic impairment is excluded. Where relevant, effective contraception is needed during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded.

support.title: Symptoms and daily life
support.text: Report injection pain with numbness or radiating leg pain, extensive bruising, jaundice or worsening symptoms.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: No routine antiemetic, steroid premedication or G-CSF is required by this endocrine monotherapy. Ask for individual symptom support.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Ask who books each check, when it is due and who reviews it. Tell the team if an expected appointment has not arrived.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: The aim is to control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer and its symptoms, with response and tolerability reviewed before continuing.

items.title: Who this card covers
items.text: The NCCP monotherapy card covers postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with relapse or progression in its specified prior anti-oestrogen setting. Companion CDK4/6 medicines require their own regimen.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 500 mg intramuscularly; individual liver-dose modification may apply. Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.

items.title: Duration and decision points
items.text: Continue while the treatment is beneficial and tolerated, with planned response reviews. There is no fixed adjuvant five-year course on this card.

items.title: Individual safety
items.text: NCCP specifies 250 mg for Child-Pugh B, whereas EMA Faslodex product information describes no mild/moderate reduction with caution. The clinician and pharmacist must reconcile this source difference. Severe hepatic impairment is excluded.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Baseline, ongoing safety checks and cancer scans have different purposes.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile. Confirm the indication, menopausal state, liver category, pregnancy exclusion and any bleeding / anticoagulant risk before intramuscular injections.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Liver profile as clinically indicated. At injection visits review symptoms, bleeding / bruising and injection-site or nerve symptoms; response imaging follows the cancer-control plan.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for fulvestrant monotherapy. Monitoring required by a separately prescribed companion drug must be added from that regimen.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Assess personal fracture and osteoporosis risk. Fulvestrant does not carry an automatic AI DXA timetable; agree testing and repeat intervals when indicated.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: Where relevant, effective contraception is needed during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded.

chapters.title: Evidence for a different decision
chapters.intro: Each study applies to its own population and treatment setting.

items.title: FALCON: separately labelled endocrine-naive context
items.text: 462 postmenopausal endocrine-therapy-naive women with HR-positive/HER 2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer. Fulvestrant 500 mg versus anastrozole 1 mg: median PFS 16.6 versus 13.8 months, HR 0.797 (95% CI 0.637–0.999). Endocrine-naive population differs from NCCP 00361's listed post-adjuvant anti-oestrogen relapse/progression indications. This trial does not broaden the card's prescribing eligibility.

items.title: FALCON final overall survival
items.text: Same randomized 462-patient FALCON population; final OS 68% mature. No significant OS difference:44.8 versus 42.7 months; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.77–1.21),p=.7579. Nonvisceral subgroup signal was not statistically significant. Do not claim a proven OS advantage. Reviewed 2025 erratum corrects author qualifications, not outcomes.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.
